You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 91c7f8ba3afc69f73da16acc673724ff299bc5da Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Paul Cercueil <paul.cercueil@analog.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2015 11:16:33 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] Network backend: fix bug introduced by 4cb089b

Signed-off-by: Paul Cercueil <paul.cercueil@analog.com>
---
 network.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/network.c b/network.c
index 2975e6ad..66a763af 100644
--- a/network.c
+++ b/network.c
@@ -240,7 +240,7 @@ static ssize_t write_all(const void *src, size_t len, int fd)
 #else
 			int err = errno;
 #endif
-			if (err = EINTR)
+			if (err == EINTR)
 				continue;
 			return (ssize_t) -err;
 		}
@@ -261,7 +261,7 @@ static ssize_t read_all(void *dst, size_t len, int fd)
 #else
 			int err = errno;
 #endif
-			if (err = EINTR)
+			if (err == EINTR)
 				continue;
 			return (ssize_t) -err;
 		}
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect assignment operator (`=`) being used instead of the equality operator (`==`) in the condition that checks if the error number (`err`) is equal to `EINTR`. This led to the condition always evaluating to true, causing the program to incorrectly handle the error case and potentially enter an infinite loop or behave unexpectedly when an interrupt occurred during system calls. The patch corrected this by replacing the assignment with the proper equality check.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect assignment operator (`=`) being used instead of the equality operator (`==`) in the condition that checks if the error number (`err`) is equal to `EINTR`. This led to the condition always evaluating to true, causing the program to incorrectly handle the error case and potentially enter an infinite loop or behave unexpectedly when an interrupt occurred during system calls. The patch corrected this by replacing the assignment with the proper equality check.
